records.title: Display on Instagram: “Christian Holzäpfel Catalog Folder, 1961, design by Gerstner + Kutter, Basel, Switzerland – from the Display Collection. #KarlGerstner…”
records.description: Christian Holzäpfel Catalog Folder 1961 design by Gerstner  Kutter Basel Switzerland  from the Display Collection. #KarlGerstner designed the H logo for Holzäpfel (Ebhausen Germany) creators of modern furniture office systems to represent both the products and the company or a schematic diagram of a room that needs furnishing. This catalog cover uses the logo in multiple variants where the thickness of the line is static and only the size proportion and boldness are changed. This result is the desire to develop something directly from within itself in the spirit of functionalism (Karl Gerstner published by Hatje Cantz 2001). by thisisdisplay

records.title: Display on Instagram: “CBS television ad “Ha, ha, ha: He laughs best, who laughs last”, 1961, design by Lou Dorfsman. From the delightful typographic forms,…”
records.description: CBS television ad Ha ha ha: He laughs best who laughs last 1961 design by Lou Dorfsman. From the delightful typographic forms elegant lettering and intelligent copy this composition is both economical and impactful and communicates a lot with little means. #LouDorfsman had a deep understanding of the network and respect for its clients. He sold the importance of statistics as an intelligent concept illustrated with each ha ha ha as a sideby-side comparison of Nielsen ratings for comedy programs.

records.description: Back in Stock! Set by Na Kim / Available at www.draw-down.com / A collection of designer Na Kims work from 2006 to 2015 published on the occasion of SET her fourth solo exhibition at DOOSAN Gallery in New York. For this book fragments of Kim's works are set in more or less personal categories taking on a form reminiscent of a sample book. In contrast with other catalogues that are linked to an exhibition published before the shows opening this book sketches the pre-exhibition content and establishes the guidelines for the imaginary stage set in the exhibition space. Designed by Joris Kritis Published by Roma Publications. First edition 2015.
